hypothesis: On native Windows anonymous pipes, a 1 ms PeekNamedPipe polling sleep yields a meaningful command-readiness tail-latency improvement over 5 ms while staying below the preregistered CPU-use ceiling during 28.57 ms idle periods.

treatment.control: 5 ms maximum sleep quantum after an empty PeekNamedPipe poll
treatment.candidate: 1 ms maximum sleep quantum after an empty PeekNamedPipe poll (production setting at frozen source revision)
treatment.only_difference: sleep quantum; both arms use the same PeekNamedPipe readiness logic and Windows API configuration

protocol.host: native Windows; record platform release and CPython version in raw results
protocol.endpoint: real os.pipe anonymous pipes, reader uses the production PeekNamedPipe API pattern
protocol.pairing: each seeded writer delay is run once under each arm; arm order is independently shuffled per pair using seed 590104
protocol.metric: write-call-start to reader observation of bytes, measured by perf_counter_ns; process CPU divided by wall duration for each idle arm
protocol.other: sequential, single-process; no model, game, WSL, or live input

decision_rule: KEEP 1 ms only if the paired per-delay p95 latency improvement (5 ms minus 1 ms) is at least 1.0 ms AND candidate idle process CPU is below 1.0% of idle wall. Otherwise HOLD; no production change is authorized by this construction.
validity_gates: all 256 latency trials receive exactly one byte and validate it
raw CSV rows and summary are independently recomputed by audit script
machine identity excludes user and checkout paths
limitations: does not establish live adapter/game/task benefit
idle CPU sample is short and host-specific
